title: One optimised kernel, its evidence, and how to put it back
description:
Stage 4's deliverable, as a document rather than as prose. Written against the real sealed artefact at cheat_for_mock/stage4-kernel-opt/kernel_optimization/, which is a KFO_MOCK=1 run: it carries the operator, the measurement apparatus and honest evidence, and it carries no `apply` and no `premise` because there was no optimisation to apply and the premise question had not been asked yet. Those two are the fields M4.3.5 and M5.1.1 add, and they are required here precisely because the sealed sample shows what a handoff looks like without them.

The document lives at `items/codes/<operator>.packup_<YYYYMMDD>/results/kernel_optimization.json`. Everything a consumer needs mechanically is in it. The packup's markdown stays, and stays commentary: `check_optimization_shape` still requires README/REPRODUCE/environment/notes because a reader needs them, but no validator and no consumer parses a number out of them.

**The reversal, M4.3.5, is expressed here and not only in the validator.** `evidence.performance.baseline.source` is `const: "workset"`: the denominator of every ratio in this document is the workset's own recorded baseline, and a schema that permitted any other value would make the rule unenforceable at rest. The old package's rule was the opposite — measure your own baseline, disbelieve the workset's — and the fields that rule needed are gone rather than deprecated.

operator.description: The `operator_id` optimised, and it must be one of the ids in the referenced workset's `operators[]`. Same pattern as `workset.schema.json#/$defs/operator/properties/operator_id`, so a value legal in one file is legal in the other.

workset_ref.description:
Which workset this was optimised against. A UUID in a README is not a reference: the sealed sample names its workset as `cd5440dc-…/v0` in prose, which no program can act on.

`snapshot` is what makes the reference checkable. A validator on m4's output phase is handed **only** the handoffs it declared in `inputs` (`validator/phase.py` `_declare_materials`, over `layout.stage(task.outputs, …)`), so it cannot reach the workset to compare against — the previous round proved that the alternative, naming the workset in `inputs`, binds the validator to the *workset's* phases and fails an innocent producer. So the handoff carries a verbatim copy, and the copy is cross-checked against the real workset in the one phase where both are staged: m5's input validation stages every one of m5's inputs, `operator_workset` among them.

digest.description: `manifest.yaml`'s `digest.sha256` of the workset handoff, or null when it could not be read. Null rather than absent: 'not recorded' and 'recorded as nothing' are different facts. Note that nothing on the consuming path verifies a digest today (`todo.md` T9), so this is provenance, not proof.

snapshot.description: Packup-relative path to a **byte-verbatim** copy of the workset's `items/codes/workset.yaml`. Fixed rather than free, because two validators and m5 all open it and a path they each read out of a field is a path they can each read differently.

premise.description:
M4.3.5, and the single most consequential block in this document.

> 优化任务的 ground truth 本身就应该严格的从 workset 中来，如果最基础的硬件、优化前提不一样，直接报错 abort。软件环境不太一样可以报 warning。

A speedup measured against a different architecture is not a smaller result, it is the answer to a different question, and the damage is that it looks entirely legitimate in the report. Measured, and this is the case the rule is written from: the sealed stage-4 run measured `B8_V151936` at 50.18 µs on gfx950 against the workset's 55.40 µs on gfx942 — 9.6% of speedup available for free, from a comparison nobody downstream could detect.

The two field lists are **copied from the workset's own `ground_truth`**, not chosen here. The workset declares what its numbers depend on; m4 does not get to decide that its own difference was the harmless kind.

abort_on_mismatch.description: Verbatim from the workset's `ground_truth.abort_on_mismatch`. Dotted paths into the two environment records, e.g. `fixed.gpu_arch`.

dtypes.description:
Verbatim from the workset's `ground_truth.dtypes` — one activation dtype per operator_id.

`dtype` is on M4.3.5's abort list and is not an environment field: it lives in each Definition's `inputs[].dtype`, and this handoff carries `workset.yaml` as its snapshot rather than the whole workset tree. Before m3 lifted it here, `check_speedup_substantiated` printed *"dtype was NOT compared here"* and skipped — honest, and one of the four abort-level fields going unchecked. Copying it makes the comparison possible at all.

workset_environment.description: Verbatim from the workset's `ground_truth.environment` — where the baseline this document divides by was measured.

run_environment.description:
**m1's `deploy_kit` record, carried verbatim** — `10_read_inputs.py` fills it with `lib.load_environment()` and observes nothing. In `e2e-flow` this should describe the machine m4 ran on, because m1–m4 share one container on one node (CONTRACT §5), and the field exists so that 'should be' is checked rather than assumed.

**It is a claim, not an observation, and the name oversells it.** Kept as-is deliberately (leader's ruling on T34, 2026-09-04): a field that silently changes meaning is worse than one that is honestly narrow. `observed_runtime` beside it is the observation.

observed_runtime.description:
**What the container actually was, observed at exec time — beside `run_environment`, never merged into it.**

m1 measured the gap on 2026-09-04: a record saying `started_at: 09:03:51Z` against a container reporting `Created == StartedAt == 09:37:18Z` with `RestartCount: 0`. A restart preserves creation time and increments the counter, so this was a *different container wearing the same name* — every field validated and the join between record and machine was unchecked. `run_in_container.sh` is the only code in this stage that touches docker and so the only thing that can see it.

**Absent when no container step ran**, which is not the same fact as an observation that matched. That is why it is optional and never defaulted.

container_id.description: The immutable id. A name is rebindable and an id is not, which is what makes the comparison possible at all.

record_claims_started_at.description: `runtime.started_at` from the record, copied here so the claim and the observation sit in one place instead of two files.

held.description: True iff `aborted_on` is empty. Redundant with it on purpose: a reader scanning for one boolean should not have to know that an empty list means yes.

aborted_on.description: Abort-level fields that differed. **Non-empty means this handoff must not claim a speedup** — see the conditional at the foot of this schema. It is not `[]` because the run was stopped: a stopped run still writes what it found, and a reader who cannot see why is back to guessing.

warnings.description: Software-level fields that differed and were tolerated. These are **also** written into `run_environment.warnings[]`, which is the channel `environment.schema.json` defines for exactly this and which carries them forward to m5. Recorded twice because the two readers are different: this list is the premise check's own record, that one is what travels.

apply.description:
M5.1.1: 优化成果是如何 apply 回 sglang，是应该严格遵循 3 的 handoff 的.

**This block is patchkit's manifest, in patchkit's own vocabulary.** m5's `apply_patch` reads `apply/manifest.json` and is a program precisely because it reads rather than judges, so m4 emits the fields that program already takes — `container_path`, `base_sha256`, `change`, `replacement` — rather than a second spelling of the same four facts that somebody has to translate. The full contract is the `CONTRACT` constant in `assets/apply_patch.task/apply.py`, and a missing block makes it print itself.

What this block adds over that manifest is `integration_point`: the workset's **declared** `edit_target`, so that the apply is provably written against what m3 published and not against whatever file the optimiser happened to open. `check_optimization_shape` compares the two and checks each `container_path` resolves to the declared source file. That comparison is the whole of M5.1.1 and it is the reason this is not simply a pointer at the manifest.

apply_mode.description:
One value, and the alternative is deferred rather than unimagined: M5.3 says the mechanism should hack sglang's registry or the import machinery rather than replace whole files, and then says 但现在就这样吧 (`todo.md` T5). A second mode would mean two proofs that the patch is live, and the proof is the expensive half.

Named `apply_mode` and not `mode` because that is what patchkit calls it. One vocabulary.

manifest.description: Packup-relative path to the manifest m5 actually opens. Fixed rather than free: `apply_patch` globs `*/apply/manifest.json` and a manifest anywhere else is a manifest it will not find. `check_optimization_shape` verifies the file exists and that its `files[]` agree with this block's, so the two cannot drift.

image.description: The image the optimisation was measured against. m5 compares it to the image it is applying into and prints a NOTE when they differ — a patch cut against one image and applied to another is not automatically wrong, and it is never automatically right either.

logical_operator.description: patchkit's name for what the operator is called in the engine, as opposed to `operator` which is the workset's id for it. The two are usually the same string and are allowed not to be.

integration_point.description: Copied from the workset's `operators[].edit_target`. `check_optimization_shape` compares it field-for-field against the carried snapshot, and separately checks that every `container_path` below resolves to this file: an `apply` written against a different file than the workset declared is the failure this block exists to make impossible.

repo_root_var.description: Three legal forms, and all three occur. `@NAME@` is what this package's `assets/lib/container_roots.yaml` writes and the only form that survives the seal — `handoff/locality.py`'s lookbehind excludes `@` but not `}`, so `${SGLANG_ROOT}/srt/x.py` leaves `/srt/x.py` as a fresh absolute-path candidate and is refused anyway. `${NAME}` is what the sealed artefact writes and is accepted so a mock of it validates. **Empty means the owner is unknown**, which is a real state rather than an omission: three of the top routable candidates on the real 124-kernel table are Triton kernels no owner rule matches.

files.description: One entry per file the overlay replaces or adds, in patchkit's shape. Mirrored into `apply/manifest.json`, which is the copy m5 reads.

container_path.description:
`@ROOT@/...` form, always. An absolute container path cannot be sealed: `handoff/locality.py` refuses content naming a path outside a small allow-list and scans every UTF-8 file, so `/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/sampler.py` cannot be published at all. The roots are in `assets/lib/container_roots.yaml`; `SGLANG_ROOT` expands to `/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang`.

The rule is right for what it defends against — a record of one machine's afternoon is not transferable — and wrong here, because a container path is a fact about an image rather than about a machine. The framework has a mechanism for exactly this and the two ends are not wired together (`temp/bugs/002-handoff-dependencies-never-reach-locality-check.md`).

base_sha256.description: The hash of the **stock** file this was cut against, not of the replacement. m5 pulls the file out of the image, hashes it, and refuses on a mismatch — which is what makes 'this patch belongs to this image' checkable rather than asserted.

replacement.description: Packup-relative path to the whole replacement file, e.g. `results/optimized_kernel.py`. **This is the half m4 uses.** m4's real artefact is a whole optimised kernel file rather than a diff, and `apply_patch` generates the diff from stock→replacement itself so that `patch_overlay` keeps one shape downstream. Do not hand-roll a diff.

patch.description: The alternative to `replacement`: a unified diff under `apply/patches/`. Legal, and not the path m4 normally takes.

runtime_marker.description: Regexes that prove the patched code was **entered**, not merely present. **Declare this if you can.** With it, m5's `check_patch_live` upgrades from *the patched bytes were on disk inside the container* to *the patched code ran*; without it that validator still passes and says in its findings what it could not show — honest, and strictly less proof that the kernel this whole stage is about ever executed.

expect.description: What m5 should expect to see, so that it can say so when it does not.

must_preserve.description: What a replacement may not change, copied from the workset's integration contract. For `sampler_vocab_softmax` that is: the signature `sampler_softmax(logits, out) -> Tensor`, an in-place write into a caller-provided `out`, fp32 in and out, a contiguous vocabulary dimension, and **no build step** — the driver imports the module directly.

revert.description: How to get back to stock. With `overlay_files` this is 'remove the overlay', which is trivial and is written down anyway: a reproducer who has to infer the undo from the do is one bad inference from a dirty tree.

evidence.description: Everything measured. Ordered as it is run: correctness first, then performance, because a kernel that is faster and wrong must never reach a timing loop.

correctness.description: The **workset's own** correctness entrypoint, run on the optimised kernel. Not a re-implementation of it, and not forge's internal SNR gate — that gate is forge grading its own homework, and it is recorded under `forge` where it belongs.

report.description: Packup-relative path to the correctness report the entrypoint wrote. It validates against `workset.schema.json#/$defs/correctness_report`, which is what makes m3's format and m4's the same format.

passed.description: **Boolean, and there is no ratio anywhere near it.** Correctness is not a percentage: a kernel that is right on two shapes of three has not two-thirds passed, it is wrong. `check_workset_runs` has a `min_pass_ratio` that forgives a minority failure and that inconsistency is recorded as `todo.md` T10; nothing on m4's side inherits it.

extra.description: Operator-specific bars. For the sampler softmax the one that matters is rows-summing-to-1 within 1e-4: these probabilities feed `torch.multinomial`, so an SNR of 130 dB with rows summing to 0.999 is a sampler drawing from the wrong distribution and no SNR threshold notices.

performance.description:
The **workset's own** performance entrypoint, run on the optimised kernel, under the **workset's own** protocol. Comparing a 5-group sample against a 3-group one is not a comparison, so the protocol is copied rather than chosen.

**What was measured and what is claimed are two objects, and the split is load-bearing.** `measured` is raw milliseconds and is always present; `claim` holds the ratios and is present only when a ratio means something. The conditionals at the foot of this schema make `claim` *unwritable* under an aborted premise or a mock, which is stronger than pinning a number: a producer cannot express the misleading thing at all.

The first draft of this schema required the ratios unconditionally, and rendering the sealed run into it produced `speedup_per_case` of 1.12 / 1.11 / 1.03 beside a `mean_case_speedup` of 1.0 — arithmetic that is *correct*, since the new rule divides by the workset's gfx942 baseline, and that reads as an 11% win on a run where nothing was optimised. A shape that forces an honest producer to publish that number is the wrong shape.

protocol.description: Copied from the workset's `protocol`. Same field names as `workset.schema.json#/$defs/protocol` so the two can be compared without translation.

timing.description:
HOW the clock was taken, not how long it ran. **This field is a COPY of the workset's `protocol.timing`, and `check_optimization_shape` compares the two with `_same` -- so it must carry exactly the values the workset schema permits, and no others.** It briefly permitted five. Four of them validated here and could never match any workset, which is a legal-but-unreachable value: an artefact that passes its own schema and fails every comparison, with nothing explaining why. Found by m4 sweeping for the field-pair class, and it was my defect -- I widened this enum to admit m3's honest correction without checking what the other end permitted.

'wall_clock_sync' is what run_performance.sh does: synchronise, start perf_counter, iters calls, synchronise, stop, divided by iters. It INCLUDES per-launch overhead and the synchronise, amortised over the group.

One value on purpose, m3's reasoning and it governs here too: adding a second means adding the code, this enum member and the workset's together, and re-measuring everything recorded under the old one. HIP event timing would differ systematically and in one direction on every case. **Two artefacts may only be compared when this field agrees**, so a method that exists only in a schema is a comparison waiting to be silently wrong.

source.description: One value, and the constraint is the point of the whole file. M4.3.5 makes the workset's own recorded baseline the ground truth; a schema that allowed `source: "remeasured_here"` would let a producer answer a different question in a field nobody reads. If the workset's baseline does not hold on this machine, that is an aborted premise (`premise.verdict.aborted_on`) and not a licence to substitute a number.

report.description: Snapshot-relative path of the workset's own `evidence.performance_report` — the file the figures below were read out of, named so a reader can check the reading.

per_case_ms.description: Read out of that report, unmodified. `check_speedup_substantiated` compares these to the snapshot's own numbers and fails on any difference: this field is where 'prove you took the workset's own baseline' is actually proven.

measured.description: What `results/optimized_kernel.py` timed at, on this host, now, under the protocol above. Raw milliseconds and no ratio: this object is a record of an experiment and is present whatever the experiment showed.

rsd_per_case.description: Relative standard deviation across groups, per case. Worth carrying because the two sides are not alike: the baseline is tight (~2%) and an optimised kernel has measured ~8% round to round on this hardware, and the cause was never identified. A reader comparing the two spreads should be able to see that without re-deriving it.

claim.description: The ratios, present **only when a ratio means something** — see the conditionals at the foot of this schema. Absent is a legitimate and common state: an aborted premise, a mock, and a campaign that found nothing all leave it out, and all three are honest outcomes rather than degraded ones.

speedup_per_case.description: `baseline.per_case_ms[case] / measured.per_case_ms[case]`, per case. Recomputed by the validator from the two tables; a figure that does not follow from them can only come from the record having been edited after it was measured.

mean_case_speedup.description: The arithmetic mean over `speedup_per_case`. Named to match forge's own field so the two can be put side by side, which is the comparison a reader wants.

noise_floor.description:
The ratio below which a result is not distinguishable from measurement spread here. **Transcribed from the workset's `operators[].noise_floor`, never chosen, and never defaulted.** A consumer with a fallback floor is a consumer that silently picks its own significance threshold on the one occasion the workset failed to state one, so `check_speedup_substantiated` compares this against the carried snapshot and refuses a difference rather than tolerating it.

The workset derives it rather than declaring it by hand: `run_performance.sh` computes `1 + 2.83 × rsd_max` from the measured per-group spread, which is the two-sample 2σ separation — two independent measurements each with relative standard deviation `s` differ by more than `√2·z·s` by chance alone — so a noisier host correctly demands a bigger win. At the ~2% round-to-round spread measured on a steady node that is ~1.057×, which is where the previous round's ~1.05× rule of thumb came from.

For scale at the other end: a null control on this class of host — the seed kernel against a byte-identical copy of itself, true ratio 1.000 by construction — returned 1.0017 / 0.9985 / 1.0018 / 1.0007, so the protocol's own floor is ~1.005×. That is not a licence to lower the bar; it bounds the protocol on identical code, while the floor above is what a *different* kernel has to clear.

forge.description: What KernelForge did, kept separate from what was measured. Forge's own `mean_case_speedup` is forge's number, measured by forge, during forge's run; it is recorded for comparison and it is never the claim.

mock.description: `KFO_MOCK=1`: no campaign was launched. A mock that is not visibly a mock is the single most misleading artefact this package can produce, because it looks exactly like a success — hence the conditional below, which forbids a mock from carrying a speedup at all.

degraded.description: A real campaign under a budget at or below 2.0 h. KernelForge silently drops Analysis to static-only and the implementer turn cap falls from 500 to 100 (`kernel_agents/cli.py:47`, `:1391` — the comparison is strictly greater). Nothing warns you, so the run says so itself. `improved: false` under a degraded budget is a **successful smoke test**, not a disappointment.

result_json.description: Packup-relative path to forge's own `forge_result.json`, copied verbatim, or null when no campaign ran.

mean_case_speedup.description: Forge's own figure. Null when no campaign ran — null and not 1.0, because 'forge did not run' and 'forge measured no improvement' are different facts.

gpu_target.description: The architecture forge compiled for. It is the architecture of **this** host, detected from the card, and never the one written in the workset's environment — that records where the baseline was measured, which is a true statement about the past rather than an instruction about now.

notes.description: Free text, and the one place in this document where prose belongs. Anything a consumer must act on has a field.

per_case_ms.description: case_id -> milliseconds. The `case_id` strings are the join key across this whole flow: the same strings appear in the workset's `operators[].shapes[].case_id`, in both of its reports, and in both tables here. `propertyNames` carries the workset's own pattern so a case id legal there is legal here.

field_mismatch.description: Same shape as `environment.schema.json`'s `warnings[]` items, so a premise warning can be written into `run_environment.warnings[]` without translation.

field.description: A dotted path into the environment record, e.g. `fixed.gpu_arch`.

allOf.$comment: M4.3.5, at rest: an aborted premise cannot carry a claim. A run whose hardware or optimisation premise differed from the workset's did not produce a smaller result, it answered a different question. The rule is expressed as `claim` being *forbidden* rather than as a cap on the number, because a cap still leaves the producer writing ratios, and the ratios are the misleading part: divide a gfx950 measurement by a gfx942 baseline and 9.6% of newer silicon appears as a per-case speedup that reads as entirely legitimate. `measured` stays required throughout — the experiment is still recorded, it is only the division that is refused.

performance.$comment: aborted premise: no claim may be written

allOf.$comment: The mock-consistency rule, moved out of a validator body and into the schema so that it holds for anyone who reads the document rather than only for whoever runs the check. KFO_MOCK=1 means no campaign was launched and no kernel was optimised, so there is nothing whose speed could be claimed. The sealed sample gets this right and says so in four separate places; the rule is here so the next one has to, and so that a mock that is not visibly a mock cannot be constructed rather than merely being discouraged.

performance.$comment: mock: no campaign ran, so there is nothing to claim
